findings.description: The inline policy grants the svc_deploy user wildcard actions (ec2:*, s3:*, lambda:*, cloudwatch:*) on Resource "*" with no conditions, giving full administrative control over EC2, S3, Lambda and CloudWatch — including data exfiltration, data destruction, and privilege escalation paths (e.g. via Lambda role creation or IAM-adjacent EC2 instance profiles).

The user relies on an aws_iam_access_key (static, non-rotating long-lived access key/secret) combined with wildcard permissions, so any leaked key grants permanent, broadly privileged API access with no expiration or MFA requirement.

The access key's secret material is surfaced through a Terraform output (svc_deploy_key_material), which stores the secret in the state file and CLI output in plaintext/recoverable form; anyone with read access to state or CI logs obtains live credentials for a wildcard-privileged user.
A permanent IAM access key is created for the deploy user rather than using short-lived roles/federation, so leaked credentials cannot be automatically rotated and remain valid indefinitely.
